public.prompt: A module reuses `const skuPattern = /^[A-Z]{3}-\d{4}$/g` and calls `skuPattern.test(value)` for each field. The same valid SKU passes once and fails on the next call. The validator only needs a whole-string yes/no result. Which correction removes the hidden state?

options.label: Keep the global flag and increment `lastIndex` before each call so the next search starts later.
Keep the global flag and retry `test` after a failure so its internal index cycles back to zero.
Remove `g` and reuse the anchored expression because validation does not enumerate matches.

answerProof.summary: Global and sticky regular expressions update `lastIndex` across match operations. A whole-string validation expression needs neither flag, so removing `g` makes repeated `test` calls independent.
decisiveConstraints: Each field validation must start at the beginning of its own string.
The expression already anchors both ends of the accepted value.
No caller needs to enumerate multiple matches.

claims.statement: Regular expressions with `g` or `y` use and update `lastIndex`, including when invoked through `test`.

optionRationales.explanation: Advancing `lastIndex` moves the next anchored search away from index zero and preserves the stateful failure.
optionRationales.plausibility: The property controls where the next global search begins, so managing it looks like the direct repair.
optionRationales.falsifyingConstraint: Every independent whole-string validation must begin at index zero.

optionRationales.explanation: A hidden retry can reset state after one failure but produces inconsistent work and obscures the first incorrect result.
optionRationales.plausibility: A failed global match resets `lastIndex`, so a second call can appear to stabilize alternating results.
optionRationales.falsifyingConstraint: One call must produce the correct result without depending on a prior or follow-up call.

optionRationales.explanation: Without `g`, the anchored validator has no progressive match index and each call evaluates the entire input independently.
